newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's MIN, Germany's Krupp renew cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's MIN, Germany's Krupp renew cooperation.

text.p: Serbia's machine industry Masinska Industrija Nis (MIN) and Germany's metals concern Krupp have agreed to renew cooperation interrupted since 1992, industry sources said Tuesday.

"Germany's Krupp will renew its cooperation with MIN and we can expect a concrete deal for making dredge transport systems for surface mines to be signed shortly and production to start within a month," MIN spokesman Miodrag Petrovic told Reuters.
MIN produced large transport systems for Krupp before sanctions and will practically only renew its former deal now, Petrovic added.
He was unable to specify the value of the deal but said it would be in the area of "millions of (German) marks".

"Krupp has in principle remained MIN's partner and is now back to continue cooperation it had with the Nis industry before war broke out in the former Yugoslavia," Belgrade daily Borba quoted Krupp representative Herbert Pannes as saying.

Krupp is interested in cooperation in the production of mine transporting machines, that MIN used to produce for it, production of chemical and petrochemical industrial facilities and production of wagons, Pannes was quoted as saying.
MIN is a machine-building giant in southern Serbia's town of Nis employing 9,000 workers. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 43 05
